description: First anonymous infill parcel in five platted blocks between Franklin and State, south of Lake and north of Randolph. Alternating open lots remain intentional.

frontage.why: T-0077, the owner's ask of 2026-08-18 on the Tremont House street scene: "there should be more and denser buildings. this is important." He sent the plate of this corner — a continuous two-storey storefront row, shoulder to shoulder on shared party lines — beside a screenshot of this same corner in the render, where the Tremont stands alone on open grass. Four of this row's anonymous roofs stood in the Clark-Dearborn block SEVENTEEN TO TWENTY-FOUR METRES behind the Lake Street frontage, each nudged off the line by its own jitter, which is the shape of a distribution and not of a street. They now stand ON the frontage: the line, its bearing and the corner they pack back from are read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and this file authors no coordinate for any of them. The 0.80 m setback is not a measurement — it is the line the two frontage buildings ALREADY standing on this face (inf_bakery_lake and inf_butcher_market) use, adopted so the street wall is one wall rather than three. No roof is added, moved out of its block, renamed or re-dimensioned: the parcel still deals 40 principal and 8 ancillary, and every id and band is the one it was.
frontage.runs: Two, and the break between them is deliberate. The corner run packs west from the block's own Dearborn corner — the two-storey store at the corner, because the corner of Lake and Dearborn is the most valuable frontage on this face and a two-storey store is what the plate puts on it, which is a typology and not a finding — and the second butts the westernmost cottage onto the standing butcher's market. Between them is a 3.6 m gangway, the width the two runs leave rather than a figure anyone chose, and the plate draws exactly such breaks between blocks of its row.

rows.note: REVISED 2026-08-13 (ROADMAP K7 phase two). These eight ancillary placements were originally spaced on the block PITCH - 314, 438, 560, 687, 810 - which put one of them at the eastern edge of every block, a building's width from the next platted street. Four of the eight reached into the roadway and the other four cleared it by 1.4-2.1 m, which is nothing against this dataset's own 20 m georeference: the four that passed were the three privies and a small shed, and they passed by being small rather than by being placed. Each now stands directly behind the easternmost principal roof of its own block - the same local E as that roof, 24 m behind it - because a rear yard belongs to a lot and a lot belongs to a house. Positions were conjectural before and are conjectural after; clearing the roadway is not standing on a recovered lot.

REVISED 2026-08-13 with the rear yards above, by the same rule and for the same reason: each of the three service buildings stands behind the easternmost principal roof of the block_interior row in its own block, 21 m behind it, rather than at the block's edge. The stable and the barn are the two largest ancillary footprints in the parcel and were the two deepest intrusions here.
